issues.title: Docs claim throw during source read always closes it; unmarshall errors don't
issues.verdictReason: source_impl::operator() in rpc_impl.hh:942-949 calls unmarshall() outside the stream_receive().then_wrapped() handler that calls close_source() (rpc_impl.hh:961-966); an exception from unmarshall propagates without close_source() ever running, so _source_closed stays false, contradicting both this doc and doc/rpc-streaming.md:110-111.
issues.scopeReason: This documentation text is new in commit 69da8f5b, which is exactly what this PR added.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: Docs claim any throw from source read releases it, but serializer errors don't; process_one_buffer calls unmarshall outside any handler that calls close_source(), so an application following the doc literally will leak the connection.
reportedAs.mattpocock-review: Doc overstates that a throw always closes the source; only failures from stream_receive() call close_source(), an exception thrown by unmarshall inside process_one_buffer propagates without closing the source.

reportedAsByRun.fable-5-1-2026-09-29/ironweave/anthropic: Docs claim any throw from source read releases it, but serializer errors don't; process_one_buffer calls unmarshall outside any handler, so an exception there leaves _source_closed false and stream_close() never runs.

issues.verdictReason: try { stream_send_empty_frame().get(); } catch (const rpc::closed_error&) {} swallows the expected outcome and would also pass if the call succeeded; the actual regression signal is the later BOOST_REQUIRE_MESSAGE(!st.put_after_close), which does work (confirmed empirically: 18/20 unfixed runs failed there), but the test would read clearer with BOOST_REQUIRE_THROW asserting closed_error directly.

issues.title: yield()-loop timing to let the batch-flush poller run is not contractually guaranteed
issues.verdictReason: output_stream::flush() with batch_flushes on just sets _flush=true and registers with the reactor's batch_flush_pollfn (reactor.cc:2909) rather than synchronously writing; nothing in the API guarantees a poller runs within N yield() calls. Empirically this proved robust (0/20 unfixed runs slipped through, 23/23 fixed runs passed across 43 total runs), so the gap is theoretical rather than observed, but check_for_io_immediately() would express the intent directly instead of relying on incidental scheduling.
issues.scopeReason: This is part of the new test added by commit 5e25ebdb.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: yield() only schedules an empty task; pollers run on their own schedule, so without the fix the test could fail either on put_after_close or on the destructor assert depending on timing.

reportedAsByRun.fable-5-1-2026-09-29/ironweave/anthropic: yield() loop does not guarantee the flush poller actually runs.

issues.title: Comment misstates why _outgoing_queue_ready becomes exceptional
issues.verdictReason: send()'s send_entry().then_wrapped() (rpc.cc:328-334) calls abort() on failure but still unconditionally does p->done.set_value() -- a failed entry never makes the chain exceptional. The actual sources of an exceptional _outgoing_queue_ready are withdraw()'s exception path from stop_send_loop() and the direct _negotiated abort (rpc.cc:203-217), not a 'failed' send_entry.
issues.scopeReason: This comment was added by commit f545c28a.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: The comment says _outgoing_queue_ready is exceptional if an entry failed, but a failed send_entry still resolves done normally; the actual causes are stop_send_loop() withdrawing queued entries and the _negotiated abort.

The comment's practical point holds but its literal wording is inaccurate, and the retained comment near rpc.cc:563-564 now sits apart from the _sink_closed_future = p.get_future() line it originally explained.
issues.scopeReason: This comment was added by commit f545c28a.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: stop_send_loop() still does when_all on _outgoing_queue_ready; also the retained comment now sits far from the line it explains and should be moved.

issues.title: Test claimed to hang or UAF if the hook throws a non-closed_error exception
issues.verdictReason: Traced connection::send(): with no timeout/cancel supplied, its only two possible outcomes are an immediate make_exception_future<>(closed_error()) when refused, or a future that always resolves successfully when accepted (send_entry()'s then_wrapped absorbs any internal failure via abort()+p->done.set_value(), never propagating an exception to the caller). There is no code path by which stream_send_empty_frame().get() can throw anything other than rpc::closed_error, so the hypothesized hang/use-after-free from an uncaught non-closed_error exception is not reachable.
issues.scopeReason: The reasoning concerns the new test added by commit 5e25ebdb.

reportedAs.mattpocock-review: If the hook throws anything other than closed_error, the exception propagates before release_close is set, so the parked data_sink::close() never resolves and the failure shows as a hang or ~sink_impl assert.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: If the hook throws anything other than rpc::closed_error, sink/source are destroyed while stream_close() and _stopped are still pending, which could surface as a use-after-free rather than a clean failure.

reportedAsByRun.fable-5-1-2026-09-29/ironweave/mattpococ: Test hangs instead of failing cleanly on an unexpected exception.

issues.title: New test is not shard-safe under --smp 2 (cross-shard write to server_factory.hooks)
issues.verdictReason: Traced loopback_socket.hh: connect() round-robins the SERVER-side acceptance via smp::submit_to(next_shard(), ...), while the CLIENT-side connected_socket always resolves back to the calling shard. With two make_socket() calls (parent client, then the stream socket) under --smp 2, the stream connection's server side is accepted and negotiated entirely on shard 1, so hook_capturing_compressor_factory::negotiate() mutates server_factory.hooks (a shard-0 stack object) from shard 1 -- a genuine unsynchronized cross-shard access. This is inert in practice because the test never reads server_factory.hooks back (matching I35), and 3 empirical --smp 2 runs showed no observable failure, but the underlying hazard is real. Note: server_done, which superpowers-review also attributes to 'the stream handler' on shard 1, is actually written by the type-1 RPC handler which runs on the parent connection's shard (shard 0, the first round-robin pick) -- that part of the claim does not hold.
issues.scopeReason: This is new test code added by commit 5e25ebdb, following an existing but still-hazardous pattern from stream_test_func.

reportedAs.superpowers-review: Under --smp 2 the loopback connect round-robins server shards, so the stream handler can run on shard 1 while writing server_done and pushing into server_factory.hooks, both shard-0 objects; noted as the same pattern as existing stream_test_func so not new.

reportedAsByRun.fable-5-1-2026-09-29/ironweave/superpowe: Stream handler test is not shard-safe under --smp 2.
